newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen Lott - Clinton needs bold budget move.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen Lott - Clinton needs bold budget move.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott on Friday called for President Clinton to make a "bold move" on the budget and warned that Republicans are working out details of their own balanced budget proposal, which they will offer if no accord is reached with the White House soon.

Speaking to reporters, the Mississippi Republican said Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici communicated a Republican budget offer to the White House this week. The offer seeks to bring the deficit at least to zero by 2002 and hopefully would leave a surplus cushion of $10 to $20 billion.

Lott said Clinton, who will appear on national television this weekend to discuss the merits of volunteerism, should talk about the budget. "I hope he won't just talk about volunteerism but will also talk about some really bold move on the budget," Lott said.

"I think progress is being made. There is movement on both sides, I think in the right direction. There is still a signficant gap. But I have been saying to both sides it is time to stop holding back now," Lott said of the budget talks.

The Republican budget offer did not include a proposal to adjust the consumer price index and leaves open the question of whether to adopt economic assumptions used by the White House or those used by the more conservative Congressional Budget Office. "This (CPI adjustment) is something the president will have to address," Lott said.

While many in Congress have agreed that the CPI overstates inflation, Republicans have been wary of making the first move on a downward adjustment for fear the public will see it as a cut in government benefits tied to the CPI and as a tax increase.
